SHOT: Straight-on e-commerce packshot, 4:5. ONE ring only, standing upright on the top face, seen from the front and a little above: the marquise and the chunky molten bar stand upright side by side, the bar rising high above the marquise's tip, and from each of them the band runs straight on DOWN in the same line and curves away behind into the loop of the ring, so the loop is seen edge-on as a narrow upright oval; nothing runs left to right behind them, on a cream plaster cube. Camera close, a little above the cube's top face, looking down at about thirty degrees. Macro-sharp on the metal.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is a phone photograph of the actual piece and the ONLY authority on what it is: copy its construction, its metal colour and its stone colour EXACTLY; it is the owner's photo of the ring worn on a finger, with a tray of other rings blurred behind: take ONLY the ring on the finger. IMAGE 2 is a closer crop of the same ring. IMAGE 2 is a close detail of the same piece. IMAGE 3 is here ONLY for the plinth, the camera distance, the background and the light: copy its cube and its framing exactly and ignore everything else about it.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: AN OPEN TOI-ET-MOI RING with a BOLD, WEIGHTY look, exactly as IMAGE 1 shows: a polished gold band that does NOT close, its two open ends side by side on top of the finger, both running in the same direction as the band. At one end ONE LARGE clear MARQUISE-cut faceted stone, about 5.5 x 11mm, in four strong gold claws, its long axis following the band. The band's other end becomes ONE long, CHUNKY molten gold BAR: a solid, glossy, organic rod, gently wavy like poured metal, about 2mm thick along its length and swelling to rounded droplet ends about 3mm across, about 25mm long. The bar is THICK: about a third of the marquise's width, a bold rod that carries one long bright highlight down its length. The marquise sits beside the lower half of the bar, and the bar's upper half rises well past the marquise's tip. The marquise and the bar lie side by side and parallel, both in line with the band; on the finger both lie ACROSS the finger. Exactly one stone, a clear marquise, never round, oval or pear; no pave, no halo; the bar is smooth polished gold with soft ripples, never a straight machined bar, never thin like a wire, never set with stones; the band does not close. The band NEVER crosses behind the marquise and the bar at right angles: never a cross or plus shape.

SCALE TEST: The marquise is about 5.5 x 11mm; the molten bar is about 25mm long, a little more than twice the marquise's length, and about 2mm thick, a third of the marquise's width, its droplet ends about 3mm across. The piece keeps its true small size against the cube, never enlarged.

GROUND: The cream plaster cube fills the lower half of the frame, large and close; flat faces, softly rounded corners, fine plaster grain. Warm cream seamless behind with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a bright moving highlight and a dark rolled edge on every curve, and every stone shows internal sparkle and a hard white point, never flat colour.

ABSENCE LIST: No hand, no fingers, no model, no fabric, no props, no flowers, no box. No second piece of jewellery. Metal: warm 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or greenish. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. The picture runs edge to edge as a crisp, clean, modern digital studio photograph, shot today on a high-resolution digital camera.
